title: My God, Accept My Heart This Day
description: My God, Accept My Heart This Day in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Matthew Bridges wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 412.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My God, ac-cept my heart this day And make it al-ways Thine That I from Thee no more may stray, No more from Thee de-cline.

lines: My God, accept my heart this day
And make it always Thine
That I from Thee no more may stray,
No more from Thee decline.
Before the cross of Him who died,
Behold, I prostrate fall;
Let every sin be crucified,
Let Christ be all in all!
Anoint me with Thy heavenly grace,
Adopt me for Thine own,
That I may see Thy glorious face
And worship at Thy throne!
May the dear blood, once shed for me,
My blest atonement prove
That I from first to last may be
The purchase of Thy love!
Let every thought and work and word
To Thee be ever given;
Then life shall be Thy service, Lord,
And death the gate of heaven.

licence: Public domain: Matthew Bridges died in 1894.
credits: Words by Matthew Bridges (1800–1894), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
